answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a refundable stake that grows with reputation, like a reef where every new polyp must anchor itself before it can feed. A fresh identity starts on a narrow ledge: it transacts only in small amounts until it builds a verifiable history of honest work. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes — the copper in the vault, so to speak — and misbehavior forfeits the bond, so a Sybil swarm becomes a money-losing proposition instead of a free one.
